title: Self-driving cars just got approved everywhere

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: What does universal approval of self-driving cars mean for our cities, ethics, and daily lives?

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Current tech uses lidar, neural networks, and real-time mapping — safe in most conditions, but not all.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: Job loss in driving sectors, privacy risks from constant data collection, and moral dilemmas in crash scenarios.

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Companies are testing fallback systems and partnering with policymakers to ensure transparency and safety.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: In 10 years, we may see seamless mobility, reduced accidents, and new opportunities in urban planning and work.

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: The road ahead is paved with innovation, but only if we steer with ethics and foresight.

video_cue: A quiet suburban street with autonomous vehicles gliding smoothly, pedestrians and cyclists safely crossing.
